questions.corrige_markdown:
**Substitution.** Let $u = \cos 3x$. Then $\dfrac{du}{dx} = -3\sin 3x$, so $\sin 3x\,dx = -\dfrac{1}{3}\,du$.

**Limits.** $x = 0 \Rightarrow u = \cos 0 = 1$; $x = \dfrac\pi3 \Rightarrow u = \cos\pi = -1$.

$$\int_0^{\pi/3} \cos^4 3x \sin 3x \, dx = \int_{1}^{-1} u^4\left(-\frac13\right)du = \frac13\int_{-1}^{1} u^4\,du = \frac13\left[\frac{u^5}{5}\right]_{-1}^{1} = \frac13\cdot\frac{1 - (-1)}{5} = \frac{2}{15}.$$

$$\boxed{\int_0^{\pi/3} \cos^4 3x \sin 3x\,dx = \frac{2}{15}}$$

**Check** with the antiderivative $-\dfrac{\cos^5 3x}{15}$: $\left[-\dfrac{\cos^5 3x}{15}\right]_0^{\pi/3} = -\dfrac{(-1)^5}{15} + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{2}{15}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the volume of the solid generated when the curve $y = x^3$ is rotated completely about the $x$-axis between the ordinates $x = 0$ and $x = 3$. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The volume of revolution about the $x$-axis between $x = a$ and $x = b$ is $V = \pi\int_a^b y^2\,dx$. Here $y^2 = (x^3)^2 = x^6$:
$$V = \pi\int_0^3 x^6\,dx = \pi\left[\frac{x^7}{7}\right]_0^3 = \pi\cdot\frac{3^7}{7} = \frac{2187\pi}{7}.$$
$$\boxed{V = \frac{2187\pi}{7} \approx 981.5 \text{ cubic units}}$$
(since $3^7 = 2187$ and $2187\pi/7 \approx 981.52$).
